expectations.text: The Daily is not a near-duplicate of the Master - each fact appears in one document unless the repetition is load-bearing for safe continuation
expectations.evidence: Verbatim overlap is low (8.1% of the Daily's 6-gram shingles appear in the Master — the text was paraphrased, not copied), but the fact set is near-fully duplicated. Whole structural blocks are restated in both: the risk register with impact/likelihood/mitigation/owner (Master §12 vs Daily §7 — same four risks: sourcing slip, wrong founding year, budget overrun, client silence); the constraints block including the full tone-of-voice rules (Master §3/§12 vs Daily §7); the next-action block with the same action, start-from, required inputs and stop condition (Master §15 vs Daily §9); the 'do not repeat' list of the same six items (Master §16.6 vs Daily §11); the continuation-sources table (Master §6 vs Daily §10); the approved trio (Master §7/§14 vs Daily §5/§8); the budget position, the copy-document location gap, and the 8-pages-vs-4 scope gap all appear in both. The Daily's genuinely unique content is limited to §1 (session objective) and §4 (previous-state → new-state). Master §16.1 itself tells Dan to read the Daily only 'if you want the detail behind the current blockers', yet the Daily holds little detail the Master lacks. Duplicating a full risk register and constraints block is not load-bearing for safe continuation, and it is a primary driver of the 36,079-char total.

suggestions.assertion: The Daily is not a near-duplicate of the Master - each fact appears in one document unless the repetition is load-bearing for safe continuation
suggestions.reason: This is the right thing to test but it is not operationalised, and a naive text-similarity check would give the wrong answer. Verbatim 6-gram overlap here is only 8.1% because the executor paraphrased, yet essentially every substantive fact in the Daily is restated in the Master. Consider replacing it with structural sub-checks a grader can verify mechanically, e.g. 'the risk register with impact/likelihood/mitigation appears in exactly one document', 'the constraints block appears in exactly one document', 'the do-not-repeat list appears in exactly one document', 'the next-action block appears in exactly one document'. Those four alone would have caught the ~16,000 chars of redundancy.

No assertion covers fabricated non-technical content. Assertion 3 is scoped to git/branch/commit/build/test/CI, so it passed cleanly while the Master invented a source-precedence rule ('a written answer from Marcus beats the live website, which beats the pitch deck') that exists in no input and is presented as an established project rule. A general assertion such as 'no rule, decision, or policy is stated as established unless traceable to a source file' would catch this class, which is arguably more dangerous in a content project than a fake commit hash.

Nothing rewards the strongest thing this run produced: it derived, unprompted, that brief.md promises 8 pages and 6 cards while content-calendar.csv tracks only 4 and 2, and correctly flagged the gap as unresolved with a budget implication. That is a real handoff-quality signal absent from the session notes, and it is currently invisible to the score.

suggestions.assertion: No section consists solely of 'N/A', 'None', or placeholder filler - unfilled sections are deleted outright
suggestions.reason: Low discrimination — any executor producing prose at all will pass it, and it passed here trivially. The real failure mode this seems aimed at is verbose sections that say nothing rather than sections that literally say 'N/A'. Consider reframing toward information density, or fold it into the size cap which already applies the pressure.

suggestions.assertion: Master Handoff Version is 1.0 (new canonical document)
suggestions.reason: Trivially satisfiable by writing one line, and it would pass on an otherwise empty document. Worth pairing with a check that the version is consistent with the incorporation log (here Master §17 correctly records the Daily as 'Incorporated into Master: Yes — v1.0, 2026-07-30').

eval_feedback.overall: The assertion set is well-targeted and discriminating on the substance dimension — all 12 content-fidelity assertions passed on genuine evidence, and the two size/redundancy assertions correctly caught the remaining defect. The gaps are: assertion 16 is semantically correct but not mechanically verifiable, fabrication is only policed on technical values, and the run's best output (the derived scope conflict) is unrewarded.
